## Frequently asked questions

**What is behavioral therapy for obesity?**

Behavioral therapy for obesity helps you understand and modify your relationship with food through counseling, coping skills, goal setting, and mindful eating. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in one Intensive Outpatient Program, led by an experienced and compassionate team of behavioral healthcare professionals.

**What does a bariatric psychologist do?**

A bariatric psychologist works with clients on the emotional and behavioral aspects of weight struggles, including binge eating, emotional eating, and chronic overeating. Our clinical psychologist and licensed professional counselors provide therapy focused on recovery and coping skills, intuitive eating, and family engagement, helping clients build sustainable habits and a healthier relationship with food.

**What does a bariatric dietitian do?**

A bariatric dietitian provides nutritional education, meal planning, and practical support tailored to your needs. Our registered dietitians lead grocery store tours, teach you how to navigate dining out, and work alongside our professional chef in cooking classes. We focus on sustainable dietary changes that fit your life, not rigid rules or restrictive meal plans.

**What therapy is best for weight loss?**

The most effective therapy addresses the behavioral and emotional patterns behind overeating. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we combine behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in one program. This comprehensive approach, delivered by healthcare professionals in four disciplines, helps clients build lasting skills. One program, not four.

**What is the mental health evaluation for bariatric surgery?**

Most bariatric surgery programs require a psychological evaluation to assess readiness and identify any behavioral or emotional factors that may affect outcomes. If you are preparing for surgery or already had it, our Intensive Outpatient Program can provide the behavioral support you need. Your surgeon decides the medical requirements, and we coordinate care with your medical providers throughout treatment.

If you have questions about our program or would like to learn more, we invite you to reach out.

Bariatric surgery counseling is behavioral health support that helps people prepare for weight loss surgery or address eating and emotional challenges after the procedure. It typically involves working with licensed therapists, psychologists, and registered dietitians to understand eating patterns, build coping skills, and develop sustainable habits around food and movement. At the Bariatric Counseling Center in San Antonio, we provide this counseling as part of our Intensive Outpatient Program, available onsite at our San Antonio facility and virtually throughout Texas. Our program includes group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and movement education. We coordinate care with medical providers and are in network with most health insurance plans, with claims processed under mental health benefits.

## Frequently asked questions

**How can I train my brain to stop overeating?**

We help clients understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy, mindful eating education, and dietary guidance from registered dietitians. Our Intensive Outpatient Program teaches recovery and coping skills you can use long after treatment ends. A licensed therapist can work with you on the specific thoughts and behaviors driving overeating.

**How do I stop my cravings and overeating?**

Stopping cravings and overeating takes more than willpower. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and mindful eating education in one program. Our team helps clients build coping skills, set realistic goals, and create a sustainable plan. You work with a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, and registered dietitians who understand the behavioral side of food.

**Why do people binge?**

Binge eating has many causes, including emotional triggers, stress, past dieting, and the way our brains respond to certain foods. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we focus on understanding those patterns and learning new ways to cope. Our behavioral therapy and counseling help clients address the underlying reasons they turn to food, not just the eating itself.

**Where does binge eating start?**

Binge eating often starts with a combination of emotional, environmental, and biological factors. It can develop after years of dieting, during stressful life events, or as a way to manage difficult feelings. We help clients trace those patterns and build healthier responses. A licensed therapist or psychologist is the right person to explore your individual history and triggers.

If you are struggling with binge eating or chronic overeating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

## Frequently asked questions

**Is Overeaters Anonymous worth it?**

OA meetings offer peer support and community, which many people find valuable. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we complement that approach with professional clinical care: licensed therapists, registered dietitians, cooking classes and movement education in one program. We work with people who attend OA, people who have tried it, and people exploring other paths.

**What is overeating a symptom of?**

Overeating can be tied to stress, anxiety, depression, binge eating disorder, or learned patterns around food. A licensed therapist or psychologist is the right person to explore what is driving it in your specific situation. We help clients understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy, dietary guidance and coping skills.

**What is the easiest way to stop overeating?**

There is no single easy fix, but understanding the emotional and behavioral patterns behind overeating is a strong foundation. We teach coping skills, mindful eating, nutritional planning and goal setting in group and individual therapy. Recovery takes time, and we provide structured support over roughly three months and 30 sessions in our Intensive Outpatient Program.

**What are the controversies surrounding Overeaters Anonymous?**

Some people appreciate OA's spiritual foundation and 12-step structure. Others prefer a clinical, evidence-based approach with licensed professionals. At BCC, we respect all pathways and do not replace OA. We offer comprehensive behavioral healthcare that can stand alone or work alongside peer support groups, depending on what fits your needs.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the best therapy for weight loss?**

The best therapy addresses the behaviors and emotions behind overeating. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we combine group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes and movement education in one comprehensive program. We help clients understand and modify their relationship with food. A licensed therapist can help you determine which approach fits your needs.

**How do I get over the mental block of weight loss?**

Mental blocks around weight often stem from emotional eating, past struggles, or anxiety about change. Our therapists work with clients to build coping skills, set realistic goals and practice mindful eating. We address the emotional side of food in both group and individual sessions. Progress takes time, but you do not have to work through it alone.

**How do I talk to someone about losing weight?**

If you are the one struggling, reaching out to a licensed therapist or counselor is a strong first step. Our team listens without judgment and helps you explore what is driving your relationship with food. If you are supporting someone else, focus on care and concern, not criticism. Let them lead the conversation and offer to help them find resources.

If you are ready to explore how counseling can support your goals, reach out to us. We are here to help.

**Who should I see for binge eating?**

At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we provide group and individual therapy with licensed professional counselors and a clinical psychologist who specialize in binge eating and other eating behaviors. Our experienced and compassionate team includes licensed professional counselors, a clinical psychologist, and registered dietitians. We accept most health insurance plans, and clients typically attend for little to no cost.

Binge eating has many different causes, and understanding your personal relationship with food is part of the work we do together. Stopping overeating on your own can feel impossible because food serves many roles beyond nutrition. Our program helps you understand and modify your relationship with food through behavioral counseling, dietary guidance, cooking instruction, and movement education. We work with you to build sustainable coping skills and a healthier approach to eating in a supportive environment.

Changing patterns around food takes more than willpower. It involves learning new coping skills, understanding emotional triggers, and building sustainable habits. Binge eating often stems from a combination of emotional, behavioral, and environmental factors. There is rarely just one cause. We work on these issues through individual therapy, group support, and practical education around food, nutrition, and mindful eating in our Intensive Outpatient Program.

A bariatric surgery psychological evaluation is an assessment that determines whether a person is psychologically prepared for weight loss surgery and able to make the behavioral changes required for long-term success. ## Frequently asked questions

**What are the top 3 most common eating disorders?**

The most common eating disorders include binge eating disorder, bulimia nervosa, and anorexia nervosa. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we work with clients struggling with binge eating, compulsive overeating, and chronic over-eating. Our intensive outpatient program provides behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and movement education in one comprehensive format led by licensed counselors, a clinical psychologist, and registered dietitians.

**What kind of therapy is best for eating disorders?**

Effective eating disorder treatment typically combines behavioral therapy with nutritional support and lifestyle education. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and mindful movement education. Our approach helps clients understand and modify their relationship with food. A licensed therapist or psychologist can recommend the specific treatment approach that fits your needs.

**Where can I find an eating disorder therapist in San Antonio?**

The Bariatric Counseling Center offers eating disorder counseling both onsite in San Antonio and virtually throughout Texas. Our staff includes a clinical psychologist, licensed professional counselors, and registered dietitians who specialize in treating binge eating disorder, compulsive overeating, and emotional eating. We provide an intensive outpatient program that runs about three months, meeting two to three times per week, and we accept most health insurance plans.

**Is there a 12-step program for eating disorders?**

Some people find support in 12-step programs for eating disorders. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we offer an intensive outpatient program that combines behavioral therapy and counseling with dietary guidance, culinary classes, and mindful movement. Our approach helps clients develop recovery and coping skills in a structured clinical setting. Clients typically attend for little to no cost through their health insurance mental health benefits.

If you are ready to take the next step, we invite you to reach out and learn how our program can support you.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is the root cause of binge eating?**

Binge eating often stems from a combination of emotional, psychological, and environmental factors. Stress, trauma, dieting patterns, and learned coping behaviors can all play a role. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our licensed therapists and registered dietitians work with clients to understand their unique triggers and develop healthier ways to relate to food and emotions.

**What is the difference between extreme hunger and binge eating?**

Extreme hunger is a physical need for food, often after prolonged restriction or intense activity. Binge eating typically involves eating large amounts quickly, often past fullness, and may feel out of control. Our team helps clients learn to distinguish physical hunger from emotional eating and develop intuitive eating skills that honor their body's signals.

**Why can't I stop overeating?**

Overeating is rarely about willpower. It often reflects deeper emotional patterns, stress responses, or a disconnect from hunger and fullness cues. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, and mindful eating education to help clients understand and modify their relationship with food. One program, not four.

If you are struggling with binge eating or chronic overeating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

## Frequently asked questions

**What is a psychological evaluation for bariatric surgery?**

A psychological evaluation assesses whether you are ready for surgery and helps identify any behavioral or emotional factors that may affect your success. At BCC, our licensed therapist or clinical psychologist conducts a thorough assessment and provides a detailed letter to your surgeon. We also offer ongoing behavioral support through our Intensive Outpatient Program.

**Why do I need a psych eval for bariatric surgery?**

Most surgeons require a psychological evaluation to ensure you are prepared for the lifestyle changes surgery requires. The evaluation looks at your relationship with food, emotional eating patterns, coping skills, and readiness for long-term behavioral change. Your surgeon uses this information to decide if surgery is appropriate and to plan your care.

**What does a psych eval for bariatric surgery look like?**

The evaluation typically includes a clinical interview with a licensed therapist or psychologist, along with written assessments that measure eating behaviors, mood, and quality of life. We review your medical history, weight history, and goals. Afterward, we send a letter to your surgeon with our findings and recommendations for any additional behavioral support you may benefit from.

**Is there an online psychological evaluation available for bariatric surgery?**

Yes. We offer virtual psychological evaluations via telehealth for clients throughout Texas. The evaluation is conducted by video appointment with one of our licensed professionals. Whether you meet with us onsite in San Antonio or virtually, the assessment is the same thorough process, and we provide the documentation your surgeon requires.

**How do I prepare for a bariatric surgery psychological evaluation?**

Be honest and open during the interview. There is no pass or fail. We are looking to understand your relationship with food, your support system, and your readiness for change. Bring a list of any medications you take and be prepared to discuss your weight history, eating patterns, and what you hope surgery will accomplish for you.

If you would like to schedule a bariatric surgery psychological evaluation or learn more about our program, we invite you to reach out.

## Frequently asked questions

**What are the 4 C's of addiction?**

The 4 C's are craving, loss of control, compulsion, and continued use despite consequences. These patterns show up in food addiction just as they do in other addictive behaviors. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we help clients understand and modify their relationship with food through group and individual therapy, dietary guidance, cooking classes, and mindful movement education.

**How can I mentally stop food cravings?**

Managing food cravings involves learning coping skills, identifying triggers, and practicing mindful eating. Our program teaches recovery and coping skills in a supportive environment with licensed therapists, registered dietitians, and a professional chef. We help clients develop sustainable strategies to respond to cravings without relying on willpower alone. Real change comes from understanding why cravings happen and having tools to address them.

**What is the most common food addiction?**

People often struggle with highly processed foods that combine sugar, fat, and salt. But food addiction is not really about one specific food. It is about the relationship someone has with eating. We focus on helping people who struggle with binge eating, compulsive overeating, and chronic over-eating, regardless of which foods are involved.

**What support groups exist for people with eating problems?**

We provide group therapy as part of our Intensive Outpatient Program, where clients meet two to three times per week for about three months. Our groups are led by licensed professional counselors and a clinical psychologist, not peer-led. This structure allows for clinical guidance alongside the peer support that makes group work so valuable.

If you are struggling with food addiction or compulsive overeating, we are here to help. Reach out to learn more about our program.

We coordinate care with your medical provider but do not prescribe or manage medication.

**Where can I get GLP-1 medication in San Antonio?**

Your primary care physician, endocrinologist or weight management specialist can evaluate whether weight loss medication is right for you. We focus on the behavioral side: helping you build sustainable eating habits, manage emotional eating and understand your relationship with food while you are on medication. We work alongside your medical provider.

**Are there support groups for people on GLP-1 medications?**

Yes. We offer group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and movement education in one Intensive Outpatient Program. Our program serves people struggling with weight loss, binge eating and emotional eating, including those taking weight loss medications. Sessions meet two to three times per week, onsite in San Antonio or virtually across Texas.

**Does insurance cover behavioral support for weight loss medications?**

We accept most health insurance plans, and our claims are processed under mental health benefits. Many clients attend for little to no cost. Coverage depends on your individual plan. Our team can verify your benefits and explain what is covered before you begin the program.

If you have questions about how our program can support you, we are here to help.

## Frequently asked questions

**What does a bariatric psychologist do?**

A bariatric psychologist helps people understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy and counseling. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our clinical psychologist and licensed professional counselors work with clients on coping skills, mindful eating, goal setting, and family engagement as part of our comprehensive program addressing obesity, binge eating, and chronic overeating.

**What kind of therapy helps with weight loss?**

Behavioral therapy that addresses the psychological and emotional aspects of eating is most effective. We provide group and individual therapy, dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and mindful movement education in one intensive outpatient program. Our approach helps clients develop sustainable coping skills and a healthier relationship with food, whether as standalone treatment or alongside bariatric surgery or weight loss medications.

**Why is it mentally hard to lose weight?**

Weight struggles often involve emotional eating, stress, trauma, or long-standing patterns with food that go far beyond willpower. That is why we focus exclusively on the behavioral treatment of obesity. Our team helps clients work through the underlying issues, build coping skills, and create lasting change through counseling, nutrition education, and hands-on support in our teaching kitchen and movement classes.

**How does bariatric surgery affect mental health?**

Bariatric surgery can bring emotional challenges alongside physical changes. Our program supports people before or after surgery by addressing the behavioral and psychological aspects of weight management. We help clients navigate the mental health side of their experience through counseling, coping strategies, and ongoing support. For questions about surgery itself, your bariatric surgeon is the best resource.

If you are looking for behavioral support for obesity or eating struggles, we would be glad to talk with you about whether our program is a good fit.

**What does a bariatric psychologist do?**

A bariatric psychologist helps people understand and modify their relationship with food through behavioral therapy. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, our clinical psychologist and licensed professional counselors work with clients on coping skills, goal setting, mindful eating, and family engagement. The best therapy depends on your individual needs, and a licensed therapist can help you determine what fits. At BCC, we provide behavioral therapy combined with dietary guidance from registered dietitians, cooking classes with a professional chef, and mindful movement education. This unique, all-inclusive format addresses the behavioral patterns that affect weight, whether you are in treatment alongside bariatric surgery, weight loss medications, or as standalone care.

**What are the potential mental health issues associated with bariatric surgery?**

Mental health challenges such as anxiety, depression, body image concerns, and disordered eating can occur before or after bariatric surgery. Your surgeon or medical provider is the person to discuss your specific situation. We coordinate care with referring medical providers throughout treatment.

The 30/30 rule is a guideline often given by bariatric surgeons, and your medical provider will explain the specific rules that apply to you. At the Bariatric Counseling Center, we help clients build sustainable eating habits through behavioral therapy, nutritional planning with registered dietitians, and mindful eating education. Our program supports people who have had bariatric surgery, are considering it, or are seeking behavioral treatment for obesity without surgery.

If you are looking for bariatric counseling in San Antonio or across Texas, we invite you to reach out and learn how our program can support you.

## Frequently asked questions

**What causes stress eating?**

Stress eating happens when we use food to cope with difficult emotions like anxiety, loneliness, or overwhelm. It's a learned behavior, not a character flaw. At BCC, we help clients understand their relationship with food and build healthier coping skills through behavioral therapy, dietary guidance, and mindful eating education in our Intensive Outpatient Program.

**How do I stop compulsive stress eating?**

Stopping compulsive eating starts with understanding the emotions and situations that trigger it. Our program teaches practical coping skills, mindful eating practices, and personalized strategies to interrupt the cycle. We provide group and individual therapy, nutritional support, and cooking classes in one program, helping clients develop sustainable tools to manage stress without turning to food.

**What are ADHD eating habits?**

People with ADHD may experience impulsive eating, forgetting meals, binge eating, or difficulty recognizing hunger and fullness cues. At BCC, we work with clients who struggle with these patterns through behavioral therapy and dietary guidance. A licensed therapist or your medical provider is the right person to discuss ADHD diagnosis and treatment options.

If emotional or stress eating is affecting your life, we're here to help. Reach out to learn how our program can support you.
